goal: Let me log what I eat and how much, with calories per entry, a browsable history and trends over time.
instructions:
App name for the person: Calorie Food Log

What success looks like: I can log a meal in seconds, see today's total calories, scroll back through past days, fix anything wrong, and see whether my intake is going up or down.

How the person will use it:
- Open the app and type what I just ate and how much. -> The entry is saved to today with an estimated calorie figure I can change.
- Glance at today's screen. -> I see each entry for today grouped by meal, plus the running calorie total.
- Tap an entry that looks wrong and edit the amount or calories. -> The entry and today's total update immediately, and the calorie figure is marked as mine.
- Open history and pick an earlier day. -> I see that day's entries and its total.
- Open trends. -> I see daily calorie totals for the last 7 and 30 days with my average per day.

What it keeps:
- collection Food entries: Hold each thing I ate so totals, history and trends can be worked out.. Fields: What I ate (text, required), Amount (text, required), Calories (number, required), Calories are an estimate (boolean, required), Meal (choice, required), When (datetime, required)

What it does:
- action log_food: Takes a description, an amount, and optionally my own calorie figure, meal and time, then saves one food entry. With no calorie figure it asks for an estimate first and marks the entry as estimated. With no meal it picks one from the time of day. (inputs: What I ate, Amount, Calories (optional), Meal (optional), When (optional); outputs: The saved food entry)
- action estimate_calories: Reads a food description and an amount in any style (weights, volumes or everyday portions) and returns a calorie figure with a short note on how it was reached. Always labelled an estimate and always editable. (inputs: What I ate, Amount; outputs: Estimated calories, Short explanation)
- action correct_entry: Changes the description, amount, calories, meal or time of an existing entry, or deletes it. Editing the calorie figure marks it as entered by me rather than estimated. (inputs: The entry, Changed values; outputs: The updated entry, or confirmation it was removed)
- action day_summary: For a chosen day, lists entries grouped by meal and gives the total calories for that day. (inputs: Date; outputs: Entries for that day, Total calories)
- action trends: Works out daily calorie totals over the last 7 and 30 days, the average per day, and whether the recent week is above or below the previous one. (inputs: Period; outputs: Daily totals, Average per day, Direction of change)

Constraints:
- Calories produced by Alpha are always shown as estimates and can be overwritten.
- The amount box accepts both weights/volumes and everyday portions.
- All entries stay on this Mac.
- Logging one entry needs no more than a description and an amount.
- No entry is changed without me asking.

Agreed assumptions:
- Calorie entry resolved: Alpha estimates from your description and amount, marks it an estimate, and you can type your own number instead at any time.
- Amount style resolved: one free-text amount box accepting both weights/volumes and everyday portions.
- Calorie figures are informed estimates, not from a food database, since no food source is connected.
- Meal is filled in from the time of day; time defaults to now; both editable.
- Everything stays on this Mac; nothing is shared.
- Daily goals, favourite meals, reminders and macros are left out of the first version and can be added later.

PLAN.md is what Alpha will check. Where it names an action, input, collection, field or label differently from the notes above, use PLAN.md's name.

Build a screen for this App (ui/src/main.tsx) using the labels PLAN.md names.
